alignments.note: Temporal preposition before an infinitive construct takes the 'when' (rule 52).
The infinitive keeps the verb with its supplied auxiliary (rules 17, 52).
Suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes the English subject pronoun (rule 18).

The waw of וְהִנֵּה is rendered 'Now' and fronted over the preposed temporal clause; 'now' is on rule 14's list and distance does not break the alignment (rules 25, 51). The competing reading marks the waw unrepresented and 'Now' added, but rule 14 forbids marking a connective added where a waw stands to license it.

The fronted prepositional phrase is the predicate of this verbless clause, so the supplied copula joins the preposition (rule 49); the unit is discontinuous (rule 25). The competing reading puts 'were' on the nominal anchor 'trees'.
The rectum's article takes the 'the' standing before its own word (rule 29).
Collective noun rendered by the plural 'trees'.
The ASV renders this min by 'on'.
'the one side' expands the demonstrative; head on the word carrying its sense rather than the supplied generic noun (rule 31), with the supplied 'the' going to the nominal expression (rule 15).
The repeated min takes its own 'on' (rule 25).
'the other' expands the demonstrative; head on the lexeme-bearing word (rule 31).

review_notes: Corrected: 'Now' is aligned to the waw of וְהִנֵּה rather than marked added with the waw left unrepresented. A waw stands in the verse, 'now' is one of the connectives rule 14 records for it, and the ASV has fronted it over the preposed temporal clause, which rules 25 and 51 allow; rule 14's added clause governs only a clause with no conjunction morpheme in it at all.
The waw's clause keeps 'behold' on הִנֵּה, so nothing else in the sentence competes for the connective.
'were' stays on the fronted preposition as the clause's predicate under rule 49; the alternative of putting it on 'trees' is named in that unit's note.
